items.text: After decades of captivity, a group of Israelites returned to Jerusalem and were encouraged by Haggai to rebuild the temple. The Lord promised, 'I will fill this house with glory, … and in this place will I give peace.' This promise extends to us when we prioritize God's work.

Rebuilding a holy people takes more than constructing a holy house. The inscription 'Holiness unto the Lord' must be engraved not just on temple walls or everyday objects, but on every heart. True holiness is an internal transformation, reflecting our devotion to God.

The Lord was displeased when the rebuilding of His temple was not a priority. His message to us is to 'Consider your ways.' Aligning our priorities with the Lord's leads to blessings, just as putting God first in our lives has always brought divine favor.

The early Latter-day Saints faced a situation similar to the Israelites in Haggai’s day. Both examples teach us about the Lord’s profound feelings regarding temples. They are sacred places where we can draw closer to Him and experience His peace.

The phrase 'holiness unto the Lord' on everyday objects and temples signifies that all aspects of life can be dedicated to God. This concept invites us to make holiness a part of our daily lives, transforming our actions and thoughts into acts of devotion.

Zechariah invites us to become more holy. He reveals that in a future day, when we dwell with the Lord, we will live in a state of holiness. This vision inspires us to prepare now to live in those conditions, bringing peace and righteousness to our communities.

Zechariah’s prophecies point to Jesus Christ, the promised Messiah. His earthly ministry and eventual Second Coming are foretold. Studying these prophecies teaches us about the Savior’s love, justice, and His role in bringing salvation to all who believe in Him.

The Lord declared, 'Be strong, all ye people of the land, saith the Lord, and work: for I am with you.' This powerful message of encouragement reminds us that God is with us in our endeavors, especially when we strive to build His kingdom and follow His will.

Zechariah's visions reveal what life will be like when we all dwell with the Lord in a state of holiness. This future day, where righteousness prevails, is something we can prepare for by living the teachings of the Savior and striving for personal holiness.

The Lord’s promise to fill His house with glory and give peace is a testament to His desire to dwell with His people. When we dedicate ourselves to building and preserving sacred spaces, we invite His presence and blessings into our lives and communities.
